title: Place composite-renderer dispatch in the view layer
decision_statement: Composite renderer selection is owned by FieldView, DocumentSection, or DocumentView under a most-specific-wins order, so different views may present the same semantic records differently; Field and Type do not carry the binding.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-036 defines three view-layer declaration sites and a total FieldView, DocumentSection, DocumentView, unbound precedence order.
The current schema attaches the presentation-only CompositeRendererBinding to FieldView.

alternatives: Keep compositeRenderer on FieldGroup or the replacement Type.
Put renderer selection on each instance.
Allow only a repository-wide renderer choice.
accepted_cost: Dispatch requires view capabilities and a precedence protocol, including an explicit baseline sentinel for cancelling broader bindings.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A Type-owned renderer would make a presentation choice appear to be semantic meaning.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Bindings, role maps, defaults, and baseline fallback give views a usable expression surface.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: The semantic layer withholds metadata that a renderer genuinely needs to interpret roles.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Retaining the FieldGroup dispatch placement would preserve a known coupling and prevent per-view variation.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The baseline sentinel, by-name defaults, and staged RFC-007 retirement preserve output during migration.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Presentation mechanisms are replaced before existing output has parity fixtures.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Type ownership would impose one arrangement on every view of the records.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Every view follows one precedence, identifier grammar, diagnostic, and fallback contract.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Per-view outputs become incomparable or cease to carry stable semantic identity.

coding_notes: Ownership is isolated from the renderer contract and baseline algorithm. This decision was independently calibrated as E256-B90; this family card retains a normal batch ID.

title: Render tables from structured composite values
decision_statement: The table renderer consumes typed list and inline-reference fields for columns, rows, cells, widths, headings, and labels rather than parsing arrays encoded inside text values.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-036 specifies the table contract over native lists and inline row records, including number-list width constraints.
The accepted rationale records the owner rule that structured values win whenever a real structure can be created.

alternatives: Continue parsing JSON arrays from string fields.
Carry renderer-only parsing and clamping rules for semantically structured values.
accepted_cost: The corpus needs a carrier migration and the renderer cannot become executable until #242 supplies inline composite instances.
derived_from: RFC-032 list cardinality and inline composite range

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Convenient text transport would keep structured meaning implicit, lossy, and renderer-dependent.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The table renderer retains zero-configuration role names and defines output for each supported format.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: A strict structure prevents legitimate content that the model cannot yet express.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Preserving the shipped JSON-in-text representation would retain silent parse and width-loss defects.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The design records corpus divergences and gates executable migration on #242 parity work.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Structured replacement lands without proving existing tables survive the cutover.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Individual renderers would continue inventing parsing, constraint, and failure semantics.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Vendor renderers retain their own role contracts under namespaced identifiers.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: One renderer contract is generalized into restrictions on unrelated vendor renderers.

coding_notes: Ratified design, not implemented carrier behavior at the captured snapshot. Output-shape decisions are separate.

title: Degrade invalid composite-renderer bindings to the baseline
decision_statement: Malformed, unknown, inapplicable, or contract-mismatched composite renderer bindings do not prevent a record or view from loading; implementations ignore the binding, emit a diagnostic, and render through the composite baseline.

sources.excerpt: Rules CR-036-1, CR-036-3, CR-036-7, and CR-036-9 require ignored bindings, diagnostics, and baseline rendering instead of load failure.
The binding schema deliberately leaves identifier grammar to runtime so an invalid value can fall back rather than fail View loading.

alternatives: Reject the whole View at schema-load time.
Silently ignore the binding without a diagnostic.
Render nothing for the failed composite field.
accepted_cost: A malformed presentation declaration can remain loadable, so conformance requires runtime diagnostics and deterministic fallback rather than schema rejection.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Failing the entire view would protect declaration strictness at the cost of losing otherwise renderable meaning.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The error is surfaced diagnostically and the semantic record is not altered or reinterpreted.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Graceful degradation normalizes broken declarations and diagnostics are routinely ignored.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: A stricter new dispatch mechanism could make previously renderable material disappear.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Reserved identifiers and binding contracts can evolve through ratified RFCs without schema enum closure.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Fallback preserves obsolete bindings indefinitely instead of prompting repair.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Either schema rejection would over-centralize renderer knowledge or unconstrained behavior would make failures implementation-specific.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The common fallback and diagnostic contract coexist with namespaced vendor identifiers.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Implementations diverge in what they diagnose or how they render after failure.

coding_notes: The load-vs-fallback choice is independently reversible from where bindings are owned.

title: Specify a normative composite baseline
decision_statement: An unbound or failed composite renders through a portable baseline with a resolved heading, ordered value blocks, ordered nested field rows, recursive inline composites, and deterministic block separation.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-036 defines the heading, block, row-order, nesting, omission, and separation algorithm for composite baseline rendering.

alternatives: Leave composite fallback implementation-defined.
Restore only named renderer dispatch and strand the undispatched majority path.
Require every composite to bind a renderer.
accepted_cost: The specification takes on detailed cross-format rendering rules and preserves some anomalous legacy heading behavior for parity.
supersedes: RFC-007 FieldGroup baseline for migrated composites

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Semantically valid composites without a renderer would have no predictable readable projection.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Nested rows preserve assignment order and identity; presentation remains outside the Type.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Baseline details begin dictating semantic structure or become the only usable presentation.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Removing FieldGroup without a successor baseline would delete the majority rendering path and corpus headings.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The baseline is expressed for the new composite-range model and permits recursive structured values.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Preserving inert anomalies prevents later correction even when parity no longer requires them.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Each renderer would invent a different terminal fallback for the same DocumentView.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Views and Themes may override or wrap the baseline through declared extension points.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: The portable baseline crowds out legitimate view-specific presentation.

coding_notes: This card covers the composite fallback algorithm, not the ordinary top-level field-row form later settled by RFC-037.

title: Standardize field-row output at the DocumentView boundary
decision_statement: DocumentView baseline rendering uses normative scalar and multi-entry field-row forms, ordering, separation, continuation, and HTML structure for markdown, AsciiDoc, text, and HTML rather than leaving those forms implementation-defined.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-037 FR-037-3 through FR-037-8 pin per-format scalar and block-list forms, ordering, separation, and continuation.
Merged srs-rust PR 786 implements the RFC-037 field-row baseline; the manifest records mergedAt 2026-07-31T22:14:02Z.

alternatives: Leave text-oriented field rows implementation-defined.
Standardize only markdown and let other committed formats diverge.
Render multi-entry values as comma-joined text.
accepted_cost: Implementations lose freedom over covered DocumentView serialization and must maintain full-format tests and coordinated export changes.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A semantically selected field set would still lack a portable, predictable reader form.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Multi-entry ordering and stable class identity preserve structure rather than flattening values.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Output syntax is mistaken for semantic meaning or constrains non-DocumentView interfaces.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Existing inconsistent output, including empty labels and untested format arms, would remain conformant.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Compatibility aliases and coordinated export correction stage visible changes.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Format contracts churn without migration windows or golden fixtures.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Two conforming implementations could emit incompatible DocumentViews for the same records.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The rule is confined to four normative DocumentView formats, leaving native UI independent.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: The shared format contract expands into unrelated native-client layout.

coding_notes: This groups the mutually dependent row grammar as one serialization contract. Empty-value policy, identity classes, and boundary scope remain separate cards.

title: Make empty-field output deterministic
decision_statement: An empty string or value sequence is absent and emits no label-only row; when a required field is absent under show-placeholder, the baseline must emit the literal portable placeholder `(empty)` rather than optionally choosing whether or how to show it.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-037 deliberately promotes the optional placeholder to a required literal form and defines empty values as absent.
The current rendered specification contains the mandatory omission and `(empty)` placeholder rules.

alternatives: Emit label-only rows for empty strings.
Keep placeholder presence and spelling implementation-defined.
Apply the DocumentSection placeholder rule to L1 View rendering too.
accepted_cost: Previously conforming implementations that omitted placeholders become non-conforming, and committed exports intentionally lose empty label-only rows.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A reader could not distinguish intentional absence handling across implementations and might see meaningless empty labels.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The placeholder applies only to required fields and does not fabricate a semantic value.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: A presentation placeholder is consumed downstream as actual record data.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Preserving the MAY and current empty-string bug would retain an acknowledged interoperability hole.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The L1 View path remains governed by its existing ExportConfig contract.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Corrective output changes are made without quantifying or reviewing export diffs.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Implementations could differ on both placeholder presence and syntax.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The rule is conditional on a locally selected DocumentSection.emptyBehavior.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A universal placeholder rule overrides context-specific author intent.

coding_notes: Omission and placeholder are coupled as the two outcomes of the same absent-field branch.

title: Separate field identity classes from display labels
decision_statement: A rendered field row's machine-facing identity class is derived from stable Field.name, never the contextual displayLabel; the visible label may still resolve contextually through FieldAssignment.displayLabel.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-037 requires srs-fieldname-* to derive from Field.name and prohibits deriving it from displayLabel.
The merged implementation carries the field name separately so the formatter does not normalize the human label into identity.

alternatives: Normalize displayLabel into the CSS identity class.
Use one string for both machine identity and reader label.
Humanize Field.name automatically.
accepted_cost: Renderers must carry separate semantic-name and contextual-label values, and authored labels can no longer implicitly rename style hooks.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A presentation label change would silently change the row's machine-addressable identity.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The visible label remains contextual and author-controlled through displayLabel.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Stable identity tokens leak into visible text or prevent useful contextual labelling.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Styles and automation would break whenever a human-facing label changed.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The forward class vocabulary uses a new srs- prefix with a scheduled compatibility window.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Compatibility classes become permanent duplicates after the scheduled cutover.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Implementations could choose different sources for the same identity class.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Each assignment remains free to choose its own displayLabel.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: The common class vocabulary becomes a global styling mandate beyond normative output.

coding_notes: The visible label-resolution rule is preserved while only the machine identity source changes.

title: Confine portable rendering rules to DocumentView emitters
decision_statement: The normative field-row forms bind implementations emitting covered DocumentView formats, including client-side DocumentView renderers, but do not bind native application interfaces that do not claim to emit a DocumentView.

sources.excerpt: Accepted RFC-037 binds covered DocumentView emissions and explicitly leaves native application UI outside the rule.

alternatives: Require all client UI to use the same DOM and class vocabulary.
Exempt client-side DocumentView renderers from portable output rules.
Leave the boundary implicit.
accepted_cost: Native interfaces may present the same records differently, so visual equivalence is not guaranteed outside a declared projection boundary.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A universal UI form would conflate a portable projection with every possible expression surface.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Any surface claiming DocumentView output must preserve the normative portable structure.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: A native client avoids conformance simply by declining to name an otherwise equivalent export as DocumentView.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: The evidence does not compare compatibility with change.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Analysts force a migration reading onto a scope decision.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Repository-wide visual coherence would unnecessarily dictate independent native client UX.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The DocumentView contract supplies one shared interoperability boundary regardless of which client emits it.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Local interfaces diverge in semantic content, not merely presentation.

coding_notes: Balanced Integrity/Expression is deliberately off-coordinate; the decisive choice is the shared-vs-local boundary.

title: Generate structural reference projections from semantic records
decision_statement: Resolved Field, Type, and value-object records are the semantic source; contributors keep narrative in published subsection records around a stable typed view slot, while tooling generates a property-table reference, optional pseudo-IDL, and schema from the resolved model.

sources.excerpt: The owner-recorded decision makes resolved semantic records authoritative, keeps narrative in published subsections, and selects a generated property table with optional pseudo-IDL and linked raw schema.
The ratified research result separates semantic structure, human explanation, and generated reference rather than rediscovering prose structure with regex.

alternatives: Continue comparing hand-authored pseudo-IDL to generated schemas.
Generate human prose from JSON Schema and make the schema canonical.
Embed raw JSON Schema as the main contributor-facing reference.
accepted_cost: The architecture needs effective-Type resolution, typed generated-view support, a complete emitter inventory, and staged residual checks before authorship can flip.
supersedes: RFC-031 hand-authored pseudo-IDL as the long-term structural reference

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A hand-maintained or schema-derived reader reference could drift from the project's semantic source.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: A property table is primary for readers, narrative remains hand-authored, and compact IDL plus raw schema remain accessible.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Model authority makes the generated or narrative surfaces too weak for contributors to understand the specification.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Retaining RFC-031's comparator would preserve duplicated sources and known blind spots.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: RFC-031 remains as a fail-closed residual gate until each generation boundary actually crosses.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: The final source flip happens before coverage, fidelity, and regeneration gates are complete.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Different authoring and output surfaces could independently define the same structure.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Narrative authors retain control around typed slots, and output profiles remain distinct projections.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A single generated surface displaces legitimate narrative context or target-specific views.

coding_notes: This is the #274 architectural decision, not the later implementation choices owned by #273/#272/#271.

title: Require publication reachability or deliberate invisibility
decision_statement: Indexed records must be reachable from an intended declared presentation, or their invisibility must be explicitly declared and tested; unpublished duplicate prose records are retired rather than treated as authoritative shadows.

sources.excerpt: The owner decision states that unpublished type-definition shadows are never authoritative and assigns shadow retirement and publication reachability to #285.
Issue #285 records six duplicate prose shadows and nine valid indexed table records that no committed presentation reaches, then defines the reachability guard.
Merged PR 283 retired the unrendered Field prose copy, repointed conformance at the published record, and exposed the broader shadow pattern.

alternatives: Accept duplicate valid records if a comparator checks one copy.
Delete every unreachable record, including unique table content.
Permit indexed invisibility without an explicit declaration.
accepted_cost: The repository must model presentation reachability, wire unique content into a view or explicitly justify invisibility, and remove convenient duplicate prose sources.
supersedes: RFC-031 per-entity choice of an unpublished canonical prose copy

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A valid and indexed record could remain semantically present yet invisible to every intended reader.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Unique content is wired into a presentation rather than deleted blindly, and deliberate invisibility remains expressible.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Reachability is mistaken for semantic authority or every internal record is forced into public output.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Keeping shadows would preserve an architecture whose checker read the wrong artifact and missed semantic prose errors.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Published narrative is retained, unique table content is preserved, and retirement is sequenced with generated coverage.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Cleanup removes content or RFC integration anchors before their successors exist.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Different tools could choose different indexed copies as authoritative without any shared publication boundary.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: A record may remain intentionally invisible when that local choice is explicit and tested.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: The reachability guard forbids legitimate non-public operational records.

coding_notes: The policy is ratified through #274, but #285 remained open at capture; implementation status is therefore not claimed.
